title: Matrices
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is a singular matrix vs non-singular matrix?
cards.a: A square matrix A is singular if |A| = 0. It is non-singular if |A| ≠ 0.
cards.hint: Only non-singular matrices possess an inverse (A⁻¹ exists ⇔ |A| ≠ 0).

cards.q: Formula for the inverse of matrix A using the Adjoint Method?
cards.a: A⁻¹ = (1 / |A|) · adj(A), provided |A| ≠ 0.
cards.hint: adj(A) = [A_ij]ᵀ (the transpose of the co-factor matrix).

cards.q: 10-second shortcut to invert a 2×2 matrix [ [a, b], [c, d] ]?
cards.hint: Swap principal diagonal entries (a ↔ d), negate off-diagonal entries (-b, -c), divide by determinant.

cards.q: Relation between Minor M_ij and Co-factor A_ij?
cards.hint: Sign is + when (i + j) is even; - when (i + j) is odd.

cards.q: Fundamental property relating A, adj(A), and |A|?
cards.a: A · adj(A) = adj(A) · A = |A| · I.
cards.hint: Holds for any square matrix of order n.

cards.q: Determinant value of adj(A) for a square matrix of order n?
cards.a: |adj(A)| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹. For order 3: |adj(A)| = |A|²; for order 2: |adj(A)| = |A|.
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET MCQ favorite! The exponent is always (n - 1).

cards.q: Determinant value of adj(adj(A)) for order n?
cards.hint: For a 3×3 matrix, (n - 1)² = 2² = 4, so |adj(adj(A))| = |A|⁴.

cards.q: Reversal laws for Inverse and Transpose of product AB?
cards.a: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹ · A⁻¹ and (AB)ᵀ = Bᵀ · Aᵀ.
cards.hint: Order strictly reverses upon taking inverse or transpose of a product.

cards.q: What are the 3 Elementary Row Transformations (ERT)?
cards.a:
1. R_i ↔ R_j (swap two rows)
2. R_i → k R_i (multiply row by non-zero scalar k)
3. R_i → R_i + k R_j (add scalar multiple of row j to row i).
cards.hint: Never mix row and column transformations in the same matrix inversion procedure.

cards.q: How to compute A⁻¹ using Elementary Row Transformations?
cards.a: Write A · A⁻¹ = I. Apply row operations on A (left) and I (right) simultaneously until A becomes I. Then A⁻¹ = B.
cards.hint: If using Column Transformations, write A⁻¹ · A = I.

cards.q: How to detect non-invertibility during row transformations?
cards.a: If any row becomes completely zero on the left-hand matrix during row operations, A⁻¹ does NOT exist (|A| = 0).
cards.hint: Board/CET trap: An all-zero row immediately implies matrix is singular.

cards.q: What is adj(k A) for a square matrix A of order n?
cards.a: adj(k A) = kⁿ⁻¹ · adj(A).
cards.hint: Trap: |k A| = kⁿ |A|, but adj(k A) scales as kⁿ⁻¹.

cards.q: What is (Aᵀ)⁻¹ in terms of A⁻¹?
cards.a: (Aᵀ)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)ᵀ.
cards.hint: Transposing and inverting can be interchanged in any order.

cards.q: Symmetric vs Skew-Symmetric matrix definitions?
cards.a:
Symmetric: Aᵀ = A (a_ij = a_ji).
Skew-Symmetric: Aᵀ = -A (a_ij = -a_ji).
cards.hint: All diagonal elements of a skew-symmetric matrix are always 0 (a_ii = -a_ii ⇒ 2 a_ii = 0).

cards.q: Determinant of a skew-symmetric matrix of ODD order (e.g. 3×3)?
cards.a: |A| = 0 (always zero for any odd order n = 3, 5, ...).
cards.hint: MHT-CET 2-second shortcut: |A| = |-Aᵀ| = (-1)ⁿ |A| = -|A| ⇒ 2|A| = 0 ⇒ |A| = 0.

cards.q: What is an Orthogonal Matrix?
cards.a: A square matrix A satisfying A · Aᵀ = Aᵀ · A = I (which means A⁻¹ = Aᵀ).
cards.hint: The determinant of an orthogonal matrix is always |A| = ±1.

cards.q: Method of Inversion to solve linear system AX = B?
cards.a: Pre-multiply by A⁻¹: A⁻¹(AX) = A⁻¹B ⇒ I X = A⁻¹B ⇒ X = A⁻¹ B.
cards.hint: Requires |A| ≠ 0. Note the order: A⁻¹ B, never B A⁻¹.

cards.q: Method of Reduction to solve linear system AX = B?
cards.a: Apply row operations to reduce coefficient matrix A to an upper triangular matrix, then determine variables by back-substitution.
cards.hint: Saves computation steps compared to inversion; highly preferred in HSC Board subjective questions.

cards.q: Co-factor expansion theorem for determinants?
cards.a:
Sum of products of elements of any row with their own co-factors = |A|.
Sum with co-factors of any other row = 0.
cards.hint: a₁₁ A₁₁ + a₁₂ A₁₂ + a₁₃ A₁₃ = |A|, whereas a₁₁ A₂₁ + a₁₂ A₂₂ + a₁₃ A₂₃ = 0.

cards.q: If A is diagonal matrix diag(d₁, d₂, d₃), what is A⁻¹?
cards.a: A⁻¹ = diag(1/d₁, 1/d₂, 1/d₃), provided d₁, d₂, d₃ ≠ 0.
cards.hint: To invert a diagonal matrix, simply invert each diagonal element.

cards.q: What is |A⁻¹| in terms of |A|?
cards.hint: Follows from |A · A⁻¹| = |I| = 1 ⇒ |A| · |A⁻¹| = 1.

cards.q: Definitions of Idempotent, Involutory, and Nilpotent matrices?
cards.a:
Idempotent: A² = A.
Involutory: A² = I (which means A⁻¹ = A).
Nilpotent: Aᵏ = O for some positive integer k.
cards.hint: If A is involutory, det(A) = ±1.

cards.q: Formula for adj(AB)?
cards.a: adj(AB) = adj(B) · adj(A).
cards.hint: Reversal law applies to adjoints just like matrix inverses.

cards.q: Shortcut sign pattern for 3×3 co-factor calculation?
cards.hint: Remember: transpose the co-factor matrix to obtain adj(A). Forgetting transpose is the #1 mistake!

cards.q: Conditions for consistency of linear system AX = B?
cards.a:
1. Unique solution: |A| ≠ 0.
2. Infinitely many solutions: |A| = 0 and (adj A) · B = O.
3. No solution (inconsistent): |A| = 0 and (adj A) · B ≠ O.
cards.hint: Essential 10-second check for MHT-CET system consistency MCQs.
